title: Elementary arithmetic — 32 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
Elementary arithmetic — 32 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the ring. 32 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide); 1 rfl declaration(s) are listed and not sealed, by design. Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 11 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 86 pair(s); the theorems fall into 14 strand(s), the largest of 13. Most binding: unitsMod (12), isPrime (4), ordMod (4), properDivisorSum (2), totient (2), powMod (2). 4 theorem(s) name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: families.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 file(s): src/proof/elementary.lean, src/proof/families.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 32 sealed receipts fold to b018e6fb-dc7a-86e7-bc49-d59e7e057f65. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (4, 5, 8, 1, 1, 4, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: flow.lean (4 observed, 1.06 expected, lift 3.76), demand.lean (8 observed, 2.84 expected, lift 2.82), reach.lean (4 observed, 1.77 expected, lift 2.25). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.57; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.57. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 4.0% of them — above chance by this measure, though with 33 clusters about two are expected there by chance alone.

Prior art. Euclid (Elements IX.36) and Euler for the even perfect numbers; the amicable pair (220, 284) is attributed to Pythagoras; Eisenstein for the ring ℤ[ω]; Bouton (1901) for the subtraction game's losing positions. None of these results is this deposit's. What is this deposit's is the DECISION of each over a stated finite range, axiom-free, and the honest record of where the range stops short of what the older claim asserted. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.
